In brief: The upcoming week in Abuja will be marked by a significant chance of rainfall, with temperatures remaining relatively steady, as a low-pressure system dominates the region, leading to increased humidity and precipitation. ### Monday The current temperature of 22°C, which feels like 26°C due to the high humidity of 98%, is expected to rise to a high of 26°C, with a low of 22°C, as the day progresses. The 93% chance of rain indicates a strong likelihood of precipitation, with models suggesting that the majority of the rain will fall in the late afternoon and evening. The wind direction will be relatively calm, at 5 km/h, which may lead to an increased risk of flooding in low-lying areas, particularly in districts such as Gwarinpa and parts of Wuse. As the rain moves in, residents in areas like Maitama can expect a significant decrease in visibility, making commuting more challenging, especially along the airport road.
The rain accumulation on Monday is expected to be in the range of 20-30 mm, which may cause some disruptions to traffic, especially in areas with poor drainage. The Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway, which is currently experiencing light traffic, may become congested as the day wears on. In areas like Garki, the increased humidity may make the air feel heavier, leading to a sense of discomfort for some residents. As the low-pressure system moves into the region, it will bring with it a mass of moist air, which will lead to increased precipitation and humidity throughout the day. The UV index of 0 indicates that there will be little to no direct sunlight, especially during the periods of heavy rain. This may lead to a decrease in temperature, making the air feel cooler, especially in the evening. As the day progresses, the rain will likely become more intense, with a higher chance of thunderstorms, which may affect the evening commute. My best guess is that the rain will clear up by the late evening, leaving behind a cooler and more humid environment. ### Tuesday On Tuesday, the high temperature will rise to 28°C, with a low of 22°C, as the low-pressure system begins to move out of the region. The 49% chance of rain indicates a decrease in precipitation, with most of the rain falling in the morning hours. The wind direction will shift, becoming more northeasterly, which may lead to a decrease in humidity, especially in areas like Aso Rock. The decrease in humidity may make the air feel cooler, especially in the morning, as the sun rises over the city.
The rain accumulation on Tuesday is expected to be significantly less than on Monday, with most areas receiving less than 10 mm of rain. This decrease in precipitation may lead to an improvement in traffic conditions, especially on the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway. In areas like the National Assembly, the decreased humidity may lead to an increase in visibility, making it easier to navigate the city. As the day progresses, the chance of rain will decrease, leading to a mostly dry evening, with a slight chance of scattered thunderstorms. The temperature will feel hotter in areas like Wuse, due to the increased sun exposure, as the rain clears up. The UV index will rise to 2, indicating a moderate level of direct sunlight, which may lead to an increase in temperature, especially in the afternoon. As the low-pressure system moves out of the region, it will be replaced by a high-pressure system, which will bring with it a drier and cooler air mass. ### Wednesday The high temperature on Wednesday will be 27°C, with a low of 21°C, as the high-pressure system begins to dominate the region. The 52% chance of rain indicates a moderate likelihood of precipitation, with most of the rain falling in the late afternoon and evening. The wind direction will be relatively calm, at 5 km/h, which may lead to an increased risk of flooding, especially in low-lying areas. The rain accumulation on Wednesday is expected to be in the range of 15-25 mm, which may cause some disruptions to traffic, especially in areas with poor drainage.
The temperature will feel cooler in the morning, especially in areas like Garki, due to the decreased humidity. The UV index will be 1, indicating a low level of direct sunlight, which may lead to a decrease in temperature, especially in the morning. As the day progresses, the chance of rain will increase, leading to a wet evening, with a high chance of scattered thunderstorms. The increased precipitation may lead to a decrease in visibility, especially in areas like Maitama, making commuting more challenging. The low-pressure system will begin to move back into the region, bringing with it a mass of moist air, which will lead to increased precipitation and humidity. My best guess is that the rain will clear up by the late evening, leaving behind a cooler and more humid environment. The increased humidity may make the air feel heavier, leading to a sense of discomfort for some residents, especially in areas like Wuse. ### Thursday On Thursday, the high temperature will be 27°C, with a low of 22°C, as the low-pressure system dominates the region. The 69% chance of rain indicates a high likelihood of precipitation, with most of the rain falling in the late afternoon and evening. The wind direction will shift, becoming more southwesterly, which may lead to an increase in humidity, especially in areas like Gwarinpa. The rain accumulation on Thursday is expected to be in the range of 25-35 mm, which may cause significant disruptions to traffic, especially in areas with poor drainage. The temperature will feel hotter in the afternoon, especially in areas like Aso Rock, due to the increased sun exposure, as the rain clears up.
